48: pub(crate) fn channel<T>() -> (Tx<T>, Rx<T>) {
49:     // Create the initial block shared between the tx and rx halves.
50:     let initial_block = Block::new(0);
51:     let initial_block_ptr = Box::into_raw(initial_block);
52: 
53:     let tx = Tx {
54:         block_tail: AtomicPtr::new(initial_block_ptr),
55:         tail_position: AtomicUsize::new(0),
56:     };
57: 
58:     let head = NonNull::new(initial_block_ptr).unwrap();
59: 
60:     let rx = Rx {
61:         head,
62:         index: 0,
63:         free_head: head,

69: impl<T> Tx<T> {
70:     /// Pushes a value into the list.
71:     pub(crate) fn push(&self, value: T) {
72:         // First, claim a slot for the value. `Acquire` is used here to
73:         // synchronize with the `fetch_add` in `reclaim_blocks`.
74:         let slot_index = self.tail_position.fetch_add(1, Acquire);
75: 
76:         // Load the current block and write the value
77:         let block = self.find_block(slot_index);
78: 
79:         unsafe {
80:             // Write the value to the block
81:             block.as_ref().write(slot_index, value);
82:             block.as_ref().note_after_push(slot_index);
83:         }
84:     }

86:     /// Closes the send half of the list.
87:     ///
88:     /// Similar process as pushing a value, but instead of writing the value &
89:     /// setting the ready flag, the `TX_CLOSED` flag is set on the block.
90:     pub(crate) fn close(&self) {
91:         // First, claim a slot for the value. This is the last slot that will be
92:         // claimed.
93:         let slot_index = self.tail_position.fetch_add(1, Acquire);
94: 
95:         let block = self.find_block(slot_index);
96: 
97:         unsafe {
98:             block.as_ref().tx_close();
99:             block.as_ref().note_tx_closed(slot_index);
100:         }
101:     }

103:     fn find_block(&self, slot_index: usize) -> NonNull<Block<T>> {
104:         // The start index of the block that contains `index`.
105:         let start_index = block::start_index(slot_index);
106: 
107:         // The index offset into the block
108:         let offset = block::offset(slot_index);
109: 
110:         // Load the current head of the block
111:         let mut block_ptr = self.block_tail.load(Acquire);
112: 
113:         let block = unsafe { &*block_ptr };
114: 
115:         // Calculate the distance between the tail ptr and the target block
116:         let distance = block.distance(start_index);
117: 
118:         // Decide if this call to `find_block` should attempt to update the
119:         // `block_tail` pointer.
120:         //
121:         // Updating `block_tail` is not always performed in order to reduce
122:         // contention.
123:         //
124:         // When set, as the routine walks the linked list, it attempts to update
125:         // `block_tail`. If the update cannot be performed, `try_updating_tail`
126:         // is unset.
127:         let mut try_updating_tail = distance > offset;
128: 
129:         // Walk the linked list of blocks until the block with `start_index` is
130:         // found.
131:         loop {
132:             let block = unsafe { &(*block_ptr) };
133: 
134:             if block.is_at_index(start_index) {
135:                 return unsafe { NonNull::new_unchecked(block_ptr) };
136:             }
137: 
138:             let next_block = block
139:                 .load_next(Acquire)
140:                 // There is no allocated next block, grow the linked list.
141:                 .unwrap_or_else(|| block.grow());
142: 
143:             // If the block is **not** final, then the tail pointer cannot be
144:             // advanced any more.
145:             try_updating_tail &= block.is_final();
146: 
147:             if try_updating_tail {
148:                 // Advancing `block_tail` must happen when walking the linked
149:                 // list. `block_tail` may not advance passed any blocks that are
150:                 // not "final". At the point a block is finalized, it is unknown
151:                 // if there are any prior blocks that are unfinalized, which
152:                 // makes it impossible to advance `block_tail`.
153:                 //
154:                 // While walking the linked list, `block_tail` can be advanced
155:                 // as long as finalized blocks are traversed.
156:                 //
157:                 // Release ordering is used to ensure that any subsequent reads
158:                 // are able to see the memory pointed to by `block_tail`.
159:                 //
160:                 // Acquire is not needed as any "actual" value is not accessed.
161:                 // At this point, the linked list is walked to acquire blocks.
162:                 if self
163:                     .block_tail
164:                     .compare_exchange(block_ptr, next_block.as_ptr(), Release, Relaxed)
165:                     .is_ok()
166:                 {
167:                     // Synchronize with any senders
168:                     let tail_position = self.tail_position.fetch_add(0, Release);
169: 
170:                     unsafe {
171:                         block.tx_release(tail_position);
172:                     }
173:                 } else {
174:                     // A concurrent sender is also working on advancing
175:                     // `block_tail` and this thread is falling behind.
176:                     //
177:                     // Stop trying to advance the tail pointer
178:                     try_updating_tail = false;
179:                 }
180:             }
